## Publication strategy

<blockquote>
Each paper answers a different question at a different scale, so a
single methodological debate can't unravel the whole stack. Reviewers
at each stage inherit peer-reviewed context from the layer below.
</blockquote>

- **JOSS package papers** — package-level DOIs for every dependency
- **JSS umbrella** — architectural rationale; downstream papers cite it
- **Scientific Data** — dataset itself as a citable object
- **Joule** — validated tool + data applied to a global synthesis
- **Science Policy Forum** — 1,500-word policy-actionable condensation
- **Ecological Economics** — the emergy methodological question, isolated
- **Nature Energy** — causal-identification argument built on the validated dataset

## What's actually blocking what

- **ORCID** blocks four items: Ecological Economics byline, Science
  Policy Forum submission, JOSS Wave 1 metadata, JSS authorship.
  Registration is free and takes ~15 minutes at
  [orcid.org/register](https://orcid.org/register). This is the single
  cheapest unlock in the queue.
- **EM-DAT / GDELT / IHME GBD credentials** block Nature Energy.
  Each is a separate access request; expect 2-4 weeks per institution.
- **Zenodo record upload** blocks Scientific Data (and populates
  `emburdensynth/R/global_data_download.R:20-24`).
- **External co-author read** is the last-mile blocker on Ecological
  Economics and Joule — analytically complete, waiting on eyes.

Everything else is writing time.
